Put links in a category by hand, see which service handles a download, and "Remove and delete files" takes the unpacked files along.

## ✨ Added

- **You can put links in a category by hand.** Right-click a package or a selection in the collector or in Downloads and pick one under Category, or None to take them out. When you add links, Options has a Category field too, so a batch lands in its category from the start. A Packagizer rule that names a category still wins. Thanks to @Kayn2106 for asking how in [#158](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/158).
- **The extension's video button has a card of its own in the settings.** For each site you pick whether the button shows there, what a click downloads (video, audio, subtitles, thumbnail or the description) and the quality and format you prefer. The arrow next to the button opens a card for each of these with every quality and format this video offers, each with its size and under its proper name, such as H.264, VP9, AAC or Opus, along with its audio languages and its subtitles as SRT, WebVTT or TTML. Audio can also come as MP3 or FLAC, and a format KnightLoader converts to says so. A pick that differs from what is already in your list downloads as a row of its own. After a send, a ring around the mark follows the download, and "Done" opens your downloads. With more than one instance online, the toolbar popup asks where the video goes. Alt+Shift+K sends the video you are watching, and the card lets you change the shortcut. Drag the button anywhere on the player or let it show only on hover. It follows your light or dark theme, turns gold under the pointer and lets a few stars fly when a video went through.
- **The thumbnail can come as JPG, PNG or WebP,** whatever format the site serves it in.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The Backend column shows who handles a download by its mark:** a debrid service's logo, a magnet for the built-in torrent client, and an icon each for JDownloader, yt-dlp, Usenet and direct downloads. Right-click the list header to switch it on. Thanks to @Kayn2106 for the idea in [#157](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/157).
- **The speed column shows how fast a debrid service fetches a torrent** while it is still downloading it to its own servers, and names the service when you point at it.
- **The video button's switch is in the extension's settings only,** no longer in the toolbar popup.
- **The password fields on the sign-in page show their name inside,** in grey, until you start typing.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **The extension's video button starts the download,** also with "Start added links immediately" off, where the video used to wait in the link collector.
- **The video button says "Already there" for a video that is already in your list,** where it said "Sent" although nothing was added.
- **The video button's menu stays open while it checks the qualities,** where it could close by itself after a few seconds.
- **A YouTube video set to 1080p shows the size of what yt-dlp downloads,** the same as "Best" where both fetch YouTube's Premium track. It showed the smaller size of another track.
- **A video wider than 16:9 names its qualities the way YouTube does,** so a 2:1 video offers its 1920x960 track as 1080p rather than 960p, and "Up to 1080p" on a 21:9 video no longer takes the 2560x1080 track that YouTube calls 1440p.
- **A video file carries the quality the menu showed,** so the 1080p track of a 2:1 video and a portrait 1080x1920 video both save as "(1080p)" instead of "(960p)" and "(1920p)", and their subtitles and thumbnail take the same name.
- **Subtitles picked as SRT or VTT come in that format from every site,** converted where the site serves another, and a TTML pick on a site without TTML keeps the site's own format and says so on the row.
- **"Remove and delete files" takes the unpacked files along.** The archive went, but the folder it had been unpacked into stayed. Now what unpacking wrote goes too, and the confirmation counts it in. "Remove" still keeps every file. Thanks to @Kayn2106 for the report in [#157](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/issues/157).
- **The browser extension keeps its pairing in a Firefox that lets it read its database but not write to it.** The toolbar popup stopped before it showed your group, and the video button said "Could not send". Thanks to @sabascos for the photos in [#156](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/knightloader/discussions/156).
- **A page's own short sounds stay off "Media on this page"** in the extension, such as YouTube's voice-search sounds.
- **A plain file behind a link without an extension downloads under its own name,** as one row, instead of going through yt-dlp as "(best).unknown_video".
- **The Flatpak opens on a PC with an NVIDIA graphics card** under Wayland, where the window could stay away with "Error 71 (Protocol error)" in the log.
